subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` be treated as a supported security enforcement contract for Telegram DMs?
rationale: Current schema/types accept the field, but changing enforcement affects security expectations and existing operator config; automation should not choose whether to enforce or retire that contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Enforce direct tools
options.body: Implement a DM-aware resolver that applies exact and wildcard Telegram `direct.*.tools` / `toolsBySender` before the agent tool surface is mounted, with regression and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Retire the surface
options.body: Remove or reject the direct tool-policy fields with doctor/docs diagnostics so operators are not given a silent non-enforcing security knob.

options.title: Defer pending design
options.body: Keep the issue open as a security/product decision while preserving current behavior and the duplicate report as evidence.

recommendation.title: Enforce direct tools
recommendation.body: Implement a DM-aware resolver that applies exact and wildcard Telegram `direct.*.tools` / `toolsBySender` before the agent tool surface is mounted, with regression and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is recent work on the shared tool-policy/security path plus current routing through the affected resolver files.
